gloss: hina dolls; dolls for Girls' Day

definitions.gloss: hina dolls; ornamental dolls for Girls' Day
definitions.explanation: Elaborate decorative dolls representing the imperial court, displayed on a tiered platform during the Hinamatsuri festival on March 3rd. They are set up to wish for the health and happiness of girls in the family.

examples.japanese: {二月|にがつ}になると{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}る。
examples.english: We display the hina dolls when February comes.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}から{受|う}け{継|つ}いだ{雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{大切|たいせつ}にしている。
examples.english: I treasure the hina dolls I inherited from my grandmother.

examples.japanese: {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{早|はや}く{片付|かたづ}けないと{嫁|よめ}に{行|い}き{遅|おく}れるという{言|い}い{伝|つた}えがある。
examples.english: There is a folk belief that if you don't put the hina dolls away promptly, the girl will be late to marry.

notes:
A compound of {雛|ひな} (small bird; doll; miniature) and {人形|にんぎょう} (doll). The dolls are displayed for {雛祭|ひなまつ}り (Girls' Day / Dolls' Festival) on March 3rd.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{飾|かざ}る (to display the hina dolls)
- {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{片付|かたづ}ける (to put away the hina dolls)
- {雛人形|ひなにんぎょう}を{買|か}う (to buy hina dolls)
- {七段飾|ななだんかざ}り (seven-tiered display)

CULTURAL NOTES:
A full set features the {内裏|だいり}{雛|びな} (emperor and empress dolls) at the top, with attendants, musicians, and ministers on lower tiers. Sets range from simple two-doll displays to elaborate seven-tier platforms. Traditionally purchased by the maternal grandparents for a newborn girl.
